# Benchmark results

**Host:** 12 logical CPUs, Intel Core i7-8750H @ 2.20 GHz, NVMe, Linux  
**Tool:** `archiveconverter` release build, CLI backend unless noted  
**Fixtures:** generated by `bench_nested` (gitignored under `benchdata/`; only *results* live in this tree)

Reproduce full matrix:

```bash
cargo build --release --bin archiveconverter --bin bench_nested
./target/release/bench_nested generate --scale full
./target/release/bench_nested run --scale full --threads 1,2,4 --level 1
```

CSV of the full nested matrix: [`full-results.csv`](full-results.csv).

---

## Full nested matrix (latest)

**Date:** 2026-07-27  
**Workload per nested archive:** ~1 000 001 small text files, ~305 MiB uncompressed content  
**Solid inner packed size:** ~11 MiB (highly compressible)  
**Conversion:** `archiveconverter convert --level 1 --threads N`  
**Outer:** non-solid 7z (append-store)  
**Nested concurrency:** size-aware (default workers from `--threads`, budget 500 M)

### Fixture sizes

| Artifact | Size |
|----------|------|
| `inner-solid.7z` | ~11 MiB |
| `outer-1.7z` | ~11 MiB |
| `outer-2.7z` | ~21 MiB |
| `outer-4.7z` | ~43 MiB |
| `outer-10.7z` | ~107 MiB |

### Wall-clock times (seconds)

| nested | threads=1 | threads=2 | threads=4 | speedup t4 vs t1 |
|-------:|----------:|----------:|----------:|-----------------:|
| 1 | **225.9** | 244.0 | 246.6 | **0.92×** (slower) |
| 2 | **459.6** | 293.3 | 300.5 | **1.53×** |
| 4 | **895.7** | 568.2 | 400.4 | **2.24×** |
| 10 | **2350.6** | 2756.3\* | 1147.0 | **2.05×** |

\*n=10, t=2 looks like a run outlier vs t=1; t=4 is clearly better.

### Takeaways

1. **Single nest:** multi-thread pack is often **slower** on million-tiny-file nests. The tool **forces pack threads=1** when there is only one nested archive, even if `--threads N` is set (nest *worker* count can still follow `--threads` for bulk extract).
2. **Multiple nests:** size-aware concurrent conversion helps. At 4 nests, **~2.2×** vs serial t=1; at 10 nests, **~2.0×** at 4 workers.
3. **vs older serial-only matrix** (same machine, earlier build without nested concurrency): single-nest t=1 was ~325 s; latest ~226 s (append-store outer + other pipeline work). Older full serial matrix is archived in the git history of local `benchdata/` only—not republished.

### How `--threads` is used

| Nest count | Pack / encode threads | Nest workers |
|------------|----------------------|--------------|
| 1 | Forced to **1** | 1 |
| 2+ | Follows `--threads` (and auto policy inside converters) | Up to `--threads` / `--nested-concurrency`, limited by `--nested-size-budget` |

## Large tool vs manual 7z (one-at-a-time)

**Workload:** ~280k files × 3 nested solid archives, CLI backend, **threads=1**, level 1  
**Method:** both paths process **one nested archive at a time** (fair disk model)

| Path | Wall time | Ratio tool/manual |
|------|----------:|------------------:|
| archiveconverter | ~188 s | **1.01×** |
| Manual 7z script | ~185 s | 1.00× |

Source: `cargo test --release --test compare_7z_cli large_tool_vs_manual -- --ignored --nocapture` (same session as Phase 3 bake-off, 2026-07-27).

---

## Phase 3 single solid→non-solid bake-off

**Workload:** 8000 tiny files, solid→non-solid, exclude `.tmp`  
**Command:** `cargo test --release --test phase3_bakeoff -- --nocapture`

| Engine | Seconds | vs CLI |
|--------|--------:|-------:|
| CLI 7zz extract+pack | 1.82 | 1.00× |
| native decode-ahead + MT(4) | 2.60 | 1.42× |
| parallel-codec pure-rust (4) | 0.39 | 0.21× |
| **parallel-codec liblzma (4)** | **0.19** | **0.11×** (~9× faster) |

Windowed pipeline: peak RAM ≈ encode window, not the whole archive.

---

## Tiny scale (smoke + manual baseline side-by-side)

**Workload:** 200 files / ~1 MiB per nest; nested outers 1 and 2  
**Manual:** one nest at a time, `-mmt=N` matching tool `--threads N`  
**Tool:** may run 2 nests concurrently when threads≥2

| nested | threads | tool s | manual s | ratio tool/manual |
|-------:|--------:|-------:|---------:|------------------:|
| 1 | 1 | 0.06 | 0.06 | ~1.0× |
| 1 | 2 | 0.06 | 0.06 | ~1.1× |
| 1 | 4 | 0.06 | 0.06 | ~1.1× |
| 2 | 1 | 0.11 | 0.11 | ~1.0× |
| 2 | 2 | 0.06 | 0.11 | **0.57×** (tool faster via concurrent nests) |
| 2 | 4 | 0.07 | 0.11 | **0.61×** |

Stored local baselines (gitignored): `benchdata/<scale>/results/manual_baseline.json` via `bench_nested baseline-manual`.

---

## Reproduce notes

```bash
# Full matrix (hours)
./target/release/bench_nested all --scale full --threads 1,2,4 --level 1

# Manual baselines then side-by-side (same threads both sides)
./target/release/bench_nested baseline-manual --scale full --threads 1,2,4 --level 1
./target/release/bench_nested run --scale full --threads 1,2,4 --level 1

# Phase 3 bake-off
cargo test --release --test phase3_bakeoff -- --nocapture

# Large tool vs manual
cargo test --release --test compare_7z_cli large_tool_vs_manual -- --ignored --nocapture
```

Fixtures and large output archives stay under `benchdata/` (gitignored). Publish only tables like this file when re-running.
